name: Ningbo
title: UTM Thickness Gauging in Ningbo: Hull and Tank Inspection
description: Ningbo thickness measurement for VLCCs, ore carriers and container ships at Beilun and Meishan: hull structure UTM, pre-purchase and pre-docking gauging.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement in Ningbo for Tankers, Ore Carriers and Container Ships
intro: Ningbo's deep-water berths at Beilun, Meishan and Chuanshan take mainline container ships, VLCCs discharging crude for the refineries on the coast and large ore carriers, often after a wait at anchorage. That pattern of laden arrivals and ballast departures creates gauging windows a superintendent can plan for. A team flown in from India boards at the berth or anchorage, measures what the ship's loading condition allows, and hands over data ready for the next survey or the yard specification.

highlights.p: Crude and ore arrive laden and leave in ballast. The useful time is after discharge, when holds are swept and ballast tanks are being worked, so the gauging is scheduled into time the ship already spends alongside.

highlights.h: VLCC thickness gauging at the jetty
highlights.p: Cargo tanks stay closed on a discharging tanker, but deck structure, external shell, machinery-space piping and segregated ballast tanks can often be measured — early data for a renewal survey or CAP preparation.

highlights.h: Readings that carry into the dock
highlights.p: A ship calling at Ningbo may well have its next docking booked across the water in the Zhoushan islands. Readings taken at a Ningbo berth are recorded so that yard and surveyor can extend them rather than start again.

port.h: Ningbo: deep-water berths for containers, crude and ore
p: Ningbo and Zhoushan operate as a single combined port, and together they handle more cargo by tonnage than any other port in the world. The Ningbo side carries the container trade and much of the deep-water bulk and liquid traffic. Beilun is the historic heart of the deep-water port, with container terminals, ore berths and crude jetties along the coast facing the islands of the Zhoushan archipelago; Chuanshan and Meishan, further east, add container capacity for the largest ships on the Europe and transpacific loops. Deep water close to the open sea is the reason so much of the region's crude and ore is discharged here rather than at the shallower river ports upstream.

The liquid and dry bulk trades shape inspection demand as much as containers do. VLCCs arrive laden with crude for the large refining and petrochemical complexes around Zhenhai, and ore carriers bring iron ore for steel mills along the coast and up the Yangtze, some of it moved onward in smaller ships. LNG carriers serve the import terminal on the Ningbo coast. A laden tanker or ore carrier cannot open its cargo spaces on arrival, so the useful window is usually after discharge: holds emptied and swept, ballast tanks being worked, and in some cases a wait at anchorage before the next fixture.

Container ships at Ningbo run on tight windows like anywhere on the China coast, but the port's position matters. Ships arriving from Europe or North America often call at Ningbo and Shanghai within days of each other, and a ship due for a renewal survey may already have its yard slot booked in the Zhoushan islands across the water. Gauging done at a Ningbo berth — deck, coamings, scrubber lines, accessible tanks — can therefore become the first stage of a survey programme that finishes in drydock nearby, with the berth readings carried straight into the docking plan instead of being repeated.

facilities.h: Beilun, Meishan and the Ningbo anchorages: gauging locations
p: On the Ningbo side the work is almost all at berth or anchorage rather than in dock. Container terminals give access to the ship's structure above the waterline and to its machinery and piping spaces. Bulk and ore berths give access to holds once discharge and cleaning are complete. Tankers at the crude jetties can usually offer deck, external and machinery-space piping work, but not cargo tank entry, because a discharging tanker is not gas-free and the terminal will not allow it. Each terminal applies its own rules for contractors boarding ships alongside, and the agent confirms those before the team arrives.

Anchorage work is common because ships wait for berths, for cargo or for orders, and a bulk carrier in ballast at anchorage is a good subject for pre-purchase or on-hire gauging with the team boarding by launch. When the gauging is part of a docking, the ship usually moves on to the Zhoushan repair yards, which we cover on a separate page; the Ningbo UTM readings feed straight into that yard plan, so the superintendent arrives at the docking with a defined steel renewal scope rather than an estimate.
list: Beilun port area — container, ore and crude berths where gauging fits around cargo operations on container ships, ore carriers and tankers.

Meishan and Chuanshan container terminals — the largest container ships on the Europe and transpacific loops; lashing bridges, coamings, deck plating and scrubber discharge lines during scheduled stays.
Crude and product jetties around Zhenhai — external, deck and piping gauging on VLCCs and product tankers alongside, with cargo tanks left for gas-free conditions.
Iron ore discharge berths — inner bottom, hopper and lower stool gauging on large ore carriers and Capesizes once holds are emptied and cleaned.
Ningbo anchorages — bulk carriers and tankers lying in ballast for orders or a berth; condition gauging for a sale, delivery or redelivery, by launch from the agent.
LNG import terminal — machinery-space, deck and ballast piping gauging on LNG carriers during their time alongside, within the terminal's safety rules.

context.h: Port state control and market context for Ningbo
p: Ningbo is a Tokyo MoU port, and the China Maritime Safety Administration carries out port state control on the foreign ships calling here. Large tankers and ore carriers draw close attention to structural condition in ballast tanks and cargo holds, to hatch covers and to fire main and deck piping. China's domestic emission control rules apply along this coast as well, and some waters restrict open-loop scrubber wash-water discharge, so scrubber-fitted ships decide their operating mode before the approach.

Commercially, the crude and ore trades into Ningbo are carried by large ships that are worked hard. A VLCC approaching its third or fourth renewal survey, or an ore carrier in a heavy trade, is watched by charterers and their vetting teams as well as by class. Owners use the discharge call to gather condition data — ballast tank and hold gauging, deck and piping readings — that lets them fix the yard scope and the extent of steel renewal before committing to a dock in the Zhoushan islands or elsewhere. Thickness readings taken in Ningbo give that decision facts instead of assumptions, and give the yard a realistic specification to plan against.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Ningbo
jobs.p: Most ship inspection in Ningbo uses the time a vessel already has to spend in port — discharging, waiting or redelivering — rather than creating extra off-hire. We fix the scope with the superintendent before arrival so the team boards knowing which spaces will be open and safe, and we keep the readings in the format the yard and class surveyor will want later.
list: Ballast tank and deck gauging on a VLCC after crude discharge at a Ningbo jetty, giving the owner early data for a third renewal survey and for CAP preparation.
Cargo hold gauging on an ore carrier at a Beilun berth once discharge and cleaning are complete, concentrating on inner bottom, hopper and lower stool plating worn by grabs and loading.
On-hire condition gauging of a bulk carrier at Ningbo anchorage before delivery into a time charter, recording hold and ballast tank condition for both parties.
Scrubber overboard and wash-water piping gauging on a container ship at Meishan, checking shell penetrations and the pipe sections most exposed to erosion.
Pre-docking gauging during a Ningbo call for a ship already booked into a Zhoushan yard, so the steel renewal estimate is ready before it docks.

logistics: The nearest international gateway is Ningbo Lishe International Airport; Shanghai Pudong, followed by the road across the Hangzhou Bay Bridge, is the common alternative. Beilun, Meishan and Chuanshan sit inside secure port areas where the ship's agent arranges passes and an escort to the gangway; for anchorage work the agent books a launch from the port. Each technician coming from India needs a Chinese business visa, and because it depends on an invitation letter and processing time, a firm discharge date, redelivery date or berth window is what lets us commit a team to a Ningbo call.

faqs.q: Can you gauge cargo tanks on a VLCC discharging at Ningbo?
faqs.a: Not during discharge. The cargo tanks of a discharging tanker are not gas-free and terminal rules do not allow entry. What can be done alongside is deck structure, external shell above the waterline, deck and machinery-space piping and, if the ship's procedures allow entry, segregated ballast tanks. Full cargo tank gauging belongs to a period when the ship has been gas-freed, normally on the way to the repair yard or in it.

faqs.q: Is Ningbo or Zhoushan the right place for our renewal survey gauging?
faqs.a: For the survey itself, Zhoushan: that is where the repair yards and drydocks are, and close-up survey is done there with staging in place. Ningbo is the right place for the preparation — pre-docking readings during a discharge call that define the steel renewal scope. Using both keeps the yard specification realistic and helps the dock period run to plan.

faqs.q: What does ore carrier hold gauging at Ningbo concentrate on?
faqs.a: Ore is dense and is loaded and discharged hard, so the inner bottom plating, the hopper and lower stool plating, and the areas around hatch coamings take the most mechanical damage and wastage. On bulk carriers with single-skin side shell, hold frames and their end brackets are added. We gauge on a grid that matches the TM report layout and add points wherever pitting or grab damage is seen.

faqs.q: Will the gauging keep the ship in port longer?
faqs.a: We plan so that it does not. Most Ningbo jobs fit inside time the ship already has — discharge, cleaning, waiting for a berth or for orders. If the agreed scope cannot be finished in that time, we tell the superintendent early which spaces are covered and which should be completed at the next call or in the yard, rather than asking for extra port time.
